L01.why: A colon followed directly by 'however,' is a nonstandard way to join a clause led by a conjunctive adverb; still a colon introducing an explanatory clause cannot be ruled out absolutely.

L02.why: 'have been' needs a plural or I/you subject and drops the past marker 'once' that A and D share, making it the odd one out, but a plural subject could make it right.

L03.why: Passive 'are determined' without a hidden plural subject and agent seems least likely, but a sentence could use it.

L04.why: 'have been' requires a plural subject while the other three are singular, so it is the outlier, though a plural subject would license it.

L05.why: 'has lain' breaks the progressive pattern of the other three, but a present-perfect context could still require it.

L06.why: Past perfect 'had remained' needs an earlier past reference point, the least likely context, but one could exist.

L07.why: Past progressive 'was transposing' is the least common tense for this kind of verb in a passage, but it is grammatical in some context.

L08.why: 'is the' is the only non-'do' auxiliary, so it is likely the outlier, though an 'is' comparison could be right.

L09.why: 'as is' is the singular 'be' form among a mixed set; it depends entirely on the hidden verb and subject, so it cannot be ruled out.

L10.why: 'were evidently' is the lone plural form among three singular options, making it the likeliest wrong answer, but a plural subject would license it.

L11.why: Plural active progressive 'were steering' depends on a plural subject and an active reading; either could hold in the hidden sentence.

L12.why: No punctuation before 'a' risks a fused sentence, though 'prices a merchant charged' is a grammatical continuation.

L13.why: A colon between a subject ending 'lazuli' and its verb 'cost' would be wrong, but if 'cost' is not the verb a colon could work.

L14.why: 'has been' breaks the simple-tense pattern of the others and needs a singular subject; still possible in context.

L15.why: Plural active progressive 'are misidentifying' is the least likely form, but a plural subject doing the misidentifying would license it.

L16.why: Plural active progressive is one cell of a 2x2 number/voice grid; any cell could be right depending on the hidden subject.

L17.why: No punctuation risks a fused sentence if 'a' starts a new clause or appositive, but 'spot a' is grammatical as a verb plus object.

L18.why: 'have been' is the only plural form, making it the outlier, though a plural subject would make it correct.

L19.why: Active progressive 'is transporting' is the least likely of the set, but an active singular subject could license it.

L20.why: 'were recording' is the only simple-past plural form; it depends on the hidden subject and time frame, so it is not certainly wrong.
